questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

With global warming on

A-the rise, we have to do

B-save the environment

C-every bit that we can to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'ACB'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence** ‘With global warming on the rise…’ **seems to be a logically correct part of a meaningful sentence. So, **A** can be the first part of the sequence.
 
• **‘we have to do…’** should follow an action. So, the next part that can follow is **C** and **part B** explains why should we do that action. So, **B **can complete the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct sequence is ACB, making option 2 the correct answer. 

***The correct sentence is-** With global warming on the rise, we have to do every bit we can to save the environment.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Great personalities (has attained) their heights by doing things differently
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'have attained'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Using **'have attained'** in place of **'has attained'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• We know that **‘Great personalities’** is **plural **in nature. So, it should be followed by the plural verb **'have*****'**, *and not by **'has'***.*
 
• The given sentence is in** Present perfect tense**
 
• **Structre:** *Sub + has/have + V₃ + object*
 
• When we use **'have*'***, the verb that follows should be in its **present perfect **form ***(-ed form)***
 
 
• ***Examples**: I have **considered** this option.*
 
 

***The correct sentence is-** Great personalities **have attained **their heights by doing things differently.*

**The correct sentence is- **The cost of a cylinder then **was** about ₹18.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Mr. Pattinson said, “I brought a chocolate for you.”

options.text: Mr. Pattinson brought a chocolate for me.
Mr. Pattinson said that he had brought a chocolate for me.
A chocolate was brought by Mr. Pattinson for me.
Mr. Pattinson said he brought a chocolate for me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'Mr. Pattinson said that he had brought a chocolate for me.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In Direct speech, the actual words of the speaker are quoted within quotation marks and in Indirect speech, we report someone **else’s** statement in our own words.
 
• When we **change the speech from Direct to Indirect**, we drop the quotation marks and use the conjunction '**that'** before the Indirect statement. We make suitable changes in tenses as well.
 
• A **simple present** becomes a **simple past**
 
 
• *Eats --to-- ate*
 
 
 
• A **present continuous** becomes a **past continuous**
 
 
• *Is eating --to--was eating*
 
 
 
• A **present perfect** becomes a **past perfect**
 
 
• *Has eaten --to-- had eaten*
 
 
 
• A **simple past** becomes a **past perfect**
 
 
• *Ate--to-- had eaten*
 
 
 
• Also, **'am'** changes to** 'was'**, '**now***' *changes to '**then***'*, '**tomorrow' **changes to '**the next day'** etc.
 
• After following the above rules:

So, keeping these points in mind, the sentence in the question, when changed from** Direct to Indirect **speech, becomes- ***Mr. Pattinson said that he had brought a chocolate for me.***

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

They ______ the storm approaching.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'saw'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Using **'saw'** in the **blank space** to make the sentence **meaningful**.
 
• The context tells us that the people could see the storm coming.
 
• Let us understand the **difference** in the usage of the words** ‘looked’ **and **‘seen’**.
 
• **Looked:** When we *look*, we make a special effort – we try to see by paying attention.
 
 
• ***Example:** I am **looking** for my book but I cannot find them.*
 
 
 
• **Seen:** When we see something, we notice it. We did not try to *see*, but that something came to our notice.
 
 
• ***Example:** I can **see** him waving at me.*
 
 
 
• So, in the given context, **‘They looked the storm approaching’** will sound **illogical**. 
 
• In the logical sense, we can eliminate **option 3** because no one will admire *(or praise)* the storm approaching.
 
• 'seen' is the V3 form of verb which can be used after** be verbs** (was, have, has, etc). As there is no helping verb before the blank, 'seen' is an incorrect option.

***The correct sentence is- **They **saw **the storm approaching.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Writing therapy posit that writing about one's (1)/feelings gradually eases the impact (2)/of emotional trauma. (3)/No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **'error lies in the part-1'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Using** 'Posits'** in the place of **'Posit'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• We know that **'Writing therapy' **is a **singular** subject and it will be followed by the **singular verb**. The given sentence in the **present indefinite**.
 
• Structure of the **present indefinite**: 
 
 
• Sub + V₁ + s/es + object ***(positive)***
 
• Sub + do/does + not + V₁ + object ***(negative)***
 
 
• **Example:** Ram **goes to** market.
 
 
 
 

**The correct sentence is-** *Writing therapy **posits **that writing about one's feelings gradually eases the impact of emotional trauma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• The word **'Posit'** means **'to suggest something as a fact or a basis for an argument or calculation'**.

 
 
• ***Example:** If we **posit** that wage rises cause inflation, it follows that we should try to minimize them.*
